run.procedureSummary:
Source: C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-w1\goodhart.md. Start: counts 3,6,6,2,2,1; all ROUTINE; tally 0. In each of cycles 1 to 5, every step finishes for all six teams before the next step starts.
Step 1, Arrivals: add the cycle's new tickets to each team. No limit applies.
Step 2, Overflow: go through teams 1 to 6 in order. If a team is over its WIP limit (10,8,12,6,9,7), set it to the limit and add the excess to the next team before that team is checked, so excess can cascade. Team 6's excess goes to the tally.
Step 3, Status check (on post-overflow counts): a ROUTINE team with count >= upper mark (7,6,9,5,7,5) becomes ESCALATED. An ESCALATED team with count <= lower mark (3,2,4,2,3,2) becomes ROUTINE. Otherwise the status holds. Each team changes at most once, and each change is logged.
Step 4, Closing: work out all amounts from the current counts first. A ROUTINE team closes floor(count/4), which goes to the tally. An ESCALATED team bounces floor(count/2) to the team upstream. All six are applied at once. Team 1's bounce goes to the tally. Limits are not enforced here.
Step 5, Backlog cut: total the six counts. Only if the total is strictly above 38, every count becomes floor(count/2), the removed tickets go to the tally, and the cycle is noted.
End: report the counts, statuses, changes, cut cycles and tally, and check that opening tickets plus all new tickets equals final counts plus tally.

openPoints.point: How the backlog cut rounds 'halved, rounding down' (is the kept amount or the removed amount rounded down?)
openPoints.assumption: The kept count is rounded down: new count = floor(n/2) and n - floor(n/2) goes to the tally. For an odd count, the larger half is removed.

openPoints.point: When bounced tickets land relative to the closing amounts
openPoints.assumption: All closing and bounce amounts come from the counts before Step 4. Bounces are added to the upstream team afterwards, so a team's own close or bounce never includes tickets bounced to it in the same step.

openPoints.point: A team that is both ESCALATED and receiving a bounce
openPoints.assumption: Its new count is pre-step count - own bounce + bounce received from downstream.
The cut fires only when the total is strictly above 38. The cycle 5 total is exactly 38, so the cut does not fire.
The checks are inclusive: >= upper mark escalates, <= lower mark returns to ROUTINE.

openPoints.point: Which counts the status check reads
openPoints.assumption: Post-overflow counts from Step 2 of the same cycle.

openPoints.point: Over-limit counts after Step 4 and Step 5
openPoints.assumption: They are left as they are until the next cycle's overflow. After cycle 5 they stay over: team 2 ends at 10 against a limit of 8, and team 4 at 7 against 6.
